subject: Are the ODE integrators exposed in function_signature.h?

messages.author: b998e9d6a5be0399
messages.subject: Are the ODE integrators exposed in function_signature.h?
parts:
Hello,

And thank you ahead of time for your help.

I wondered why the integrate_ode and integrate_ode_cvode functions do not appear in the function_signatures.h file. 

As described in an older post, I am writing C++ functions, which I want to contribute to Stan/math. These functions treat compartment models, used in Pharmacometrics. Aside from a few simple cases, where an analytical solution can be worked out, most models require a system of ODEs to be solved. I was very excited when the CV_ODE solver was released in the development branch of CmdStan. 

I am writing a function that uses the integrate_ode_cvode function, but I do not know how to expose it to Stan. The main difficulty comes from the first variable of the integrator function, f. In a .stan file, f is a user-defined function describing a system of ODE, and in C++ it is a functor. If I understand correctly this functor is constructed when .stan is translated into C++. 

The function I am writing has that argument f, which it passes on when it calls integrate_ode_cvode. How can I add my function to function_signatures.h using the ADD function? Or is there another way I should use to expose a function?

Thank you!

best,
charles

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Are the ODE integrators exposed in function_signature.h?
parts:
No, they're built into the statement grammar directly. The reason
for that is that our regular functions allow any combination of
data (double) and autodiff (stan::math::var) types to be mixed
as arguments. The ODE integrators require some of those to be data
and additionally require the name of a function to be passed in;
we don't have higher-order functions in the language (yet, anyway).

I believe our develop branch now has two such functions, one for
the Runge-Kutta solver from Boost and one for the CVODE solver
from Sundials. At least I'm seeing sundials in my builds!

There's a fair number of places that need to change with it built
into the language like this, but it's not too bad. If you get stuck
with something, let us know.

And it's great to hear you could get your function implemented.

- Bob

As a test, I wrote a replica of the integrate_ode function (same function but different name), and added new lines of codes for this replica everywhere where integrate_ode appeared (I omitted test files). I found that the following files had to be modified:

math.hpp
ast.hpp

generator.hpp

After completing these modifications, I built CmdStan (using make build), and was able to call and run the replica. I modified six grammar files (ast.hpp, ast_def.cpp, generator.hpp, term_grammar.hpp, term_grammar_def.hpp, and var_decls_grammar_def.hpp), adding the GeneralCpt function everywhere where I found the cvode integrator, and doing what seemed to be appropriate modifications. I'm not sure how telling this is, but I suspect the error might lie in one of these two files. 

I have attached the six modified grammar files. 

Thank you for your help! 

best,
charles

I am now almost certain that the lines I pasted last week are the ones causing the error messages. Specifically the "length" of GeneralCptModel_CVODE_r exceeds a maximum, that seems to be 10 arguments. If I delete the last three > expression_g(_r1), I am able to build CmdStan and the GeneralCpt function seems properly exposed to Stan's grammar. 

Is there a manageable way around this 10 arguments limit, or is this a constraint I should work with?
